test: Matched every row against the MS relator y^-(n+1) x^-1 y^n x in all spellings.
res: 3,363 rows are MS(n,w), n = 1..10, 1,006 second words. They hold most of the 2,672 unsolved rows. Rows in a family share a relator, which is why borrowed roads work.
next: Group work by family, not by row.
q: Are the unsolved MS rows solvable at all? Some may be genuinely hard open cases.

test: 10 second words solved for every n = 3..10; records 2^(n+1) + small (YXyXyx: 32 ... 2088). Our own paths on made-up rows MS(n, YXXyx): n=3 29 (on the formula), n=4 55 (formula about 47).
res: Mechanism found: a Baumslag–Solitar relation y^-1 x^2 y = x doubles a run of x's with the move pair (5, 11), then move 2 peels it one letter at a time. 68 chain rows are held by 1-2 teams; each tie ≈ 2 points (AC + Stable AC). Exact MS(3, YXXyx) = 28 at cap 20 (one under the formula): builds X^6 at 1 move per x, then y = x^7 and y = x^6 collapse in one move. The 10 chains share one construction: record gaps to the YXXyx chain are 4-28 moves and grow 1-3 per level.
next: Exact n=4 search to find the leaders' shorter prefix; then a generator path(n) for n up to 10. Luna takes the other 9 chains.
q: How do the leaders avoid our 2^(n-1) phase-A build?

test: Checked the core identity: H = S + K (S symmetric, K skew) gives [H,H^T] = -2[S,K].
res: Holds to 1e-15 (n = 3, 6, 10). It is the same identity behind the paper's 'non-normality energy = move Dirichlet form'. For search, the relator commutator load |[r0,r1]| already predicts hump height (+0.36).
